pr_title: Publish verified Oyatie API contract surface
summary: F9 product/plan review for PR #1: the bootstrap created useful contract surface, but as a 1070-file main-targeted import it is not a reusable ChangeSet/IP adoption pattern. Highest severity BLOCKER.

findings.issue: PR #1 imported the repository as a 1070-file bootstrap instead of a ChangeSet-sized implementation packet. Current masterplan contract requires every ImplementationPlan to be independently claimable/verifiable/promotable and to split unrelated lock scopes; product roadmap consumers cannot infer which M01/M02/M-CC IPs are actually advanced by this one PR.
findings.remediation: Backfill a machine-readable PR #1 decomposition map that groups each shipped contract/crate/doc cluster to the owning milestone/phase/IP and marks PR #1 as bootstrap-only, not a valid future PR template. Open bounded FixupTasks for any group without a current IP owner.

findings.issue: PR #1 targeted `main`, while the current Oya VCS roadmap expects dev→staging→production release trains before broad M01/M02/M03 fan-out. Leaving the bootstrap unannotated makes historical main-targeted PRs easy to copy into the Foundry pipeline by mistake.
findings.remediation: Record the branch-pipeline cutover in a compact migration note and require future large implementation PRs to target `dev` or carry an explicit pre-cutover exception.

findings.file: GitHub PR #1 file list: contracts/openapi/**, contracts/asyncapi/**, contracts/proto/**
findings.issue: The published API surface is adoption-relevant, but the PR did not ship a small endpoint-to-product/owner/readiness index beside the contracts. New adopters can see many APIs but cannot tell which are preview, blocked, or tied to a roadmap axis without manually traversing catalog and masterplan files.
findings.remediation: Generate a contract adoption index keyed by operation/topic/proto package with product axis, owner team, maturity, auth posture, and owning IP; wire it to the existing contract/documentation inventory gate.
